domanda: A compliance officer asks how far back you can look at CPU utilization data for a virtual machine directly in Azure Monitor Metrics, without configuring any additional collection. For how long does Azure Monitor retain platform metrics?
spiegazione: Correct: Azure Monitor stores platform and custom metrics for 93 days. This retention applies automatically with no configuration or cost for platform metrics. Why the others are wrong: '30 days' is the maximum span you can display on a single chart in metrics explorer (you can pan the chart to reach the rest of the 93-day window), not the retention period. '90 days' is the default retention of the Azure activity log, not of metrics. '18 months' is the retention for Prometheus metrics stored in an Azure Monitor workspace, which is a separate store from Azure Monitor Metrics.

sotto_argomento: Configure log settings in Azure Monitor
domanda: Your team wants to route the resource logs of a single Azure key vault to several independent destinations, and each team owns its own Log Analytics workspace. What is the maximum number of diagnostic settings you can create on a single Azure resource?
spiegazione: Correct: Each Azure resource can have up to five diagnostic settings. Because a single diagnostic setting can define no more than one destination of each type, you create multiple settings when you need to send data to two or more Log Analytics workspaces. Why the others are wrong: '1' reflects the outdated legacy behaviour where only a single setting existed per resource; multiple settings have been supported for years. '3' is not a documented limit and is often confused with the three classic destination types (workspace, storage, event hub). '10' exceeds the documented per-resource limit of five.

sotto_argomento: Configure log settings in Azure Monitor
domanda: An application team must correlate Azure Application Gateway resource logs with data from other Azure services by writing Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries, and must raise log alerts when specific patterns appear. You are creating a diagnostic setting for the application gateway. Which destination meets both requirements?
spiegazione: Correct: A Log Analytics workspace is the only diagnostic setting destination that lets you retrieve data with KQL log queries, build workbooks, and create log alert rules on the ingested records. Why the others are wrong: An Azure Storage account is intended for archival, static analysis, and backup; logs land as PT1H.json blobs and cannot be queried with KQL or used as the source of a log alert rule. An Azure Event Hubs namespace streams the data out of Azure to external systems such as a third-party SIEM; it provides no query engine or alerting. An Azure Monitor partner solution forwards data to a non-Microsoft observability platform, so any querying and alerting happens in that partner product, not through Azure Monitor log alerts.
tags: azure monitor,diagnostic settings,log analytics workspace,kql,log alerts

domanda: While investigating an incident in Azure Monitor metrics explorer, you need a chart that shows how many measurements a resource emitted during each aggregation interval, ignoring the numeric value of those measurements. Which aggregation type should you select?
spiegazione: Correct: The Count aggregation returns the number of measurements captured during the aggregation interval. Count does not look at the value of each measurement, only at the number of records. Why the others are wrong: Sum adds up the values captured during the interval, so it is influenced by the magnitude of each measurement; it only equals Count in the special case where every measurement is captured with the value 1. Average is the sum of the values divided by the count, so it depends on the values. Max returns the largest single value captured during the interval, which again depends on the values rather than the number of records.

sotto_argomento: Configure log settings in Azure Monitor
domanda: Contoso runs an Azure SQL database in the West Europe region. For long-term archival you attempt to create a diagnostic setting that sends the database resource logs to an existing Standard general-purpose v2 storage account located in North Europe, but the storage account cannot be selected as a destination. You must archive the logs to Azure Storage with the least administrative effort. What should you do?
opzione_a: Create a Standard storage account in the West Europe region and select it as the destination.
opzione_b: Create a Premium block blob storage account in North Europe and select it as the destination.
opzione_c: Enable the Allow trusted Microsoft services exception on the North Europe storage account.
opzione_d: Create a second diagnostic setting on the database that targets the North Europe storage account.
spiegazione: Correct: For a regional resource, an Azure Storage account destination must be in the same region as the monitored resource. Because the SQL database is in West Europe, you must create a Standard storage account in West Europe. Why the others are wrong: A Premium block blob storage account is explicitly unsupported as a diagnostic setting destination (only Standard storage accounts are supported), and it would still be in the wrong region. The Allow trusted Microsoft services exception solves a different problem: it lets diagnostic settings reach a storage account whose firewall or virtual network rules are enabled. It does not lift the same-region requirement. Creating an additional diagnostic setting does not help, because the per-setting region requirement is identical no matter how many settings you create.

domanda: In metrics explorer you chart the Transactions metric of a storage account and apply splitting on the ResponseType dimension, which correctly shows a separate line per response type. You then create a diagnostic setting that sends AllMetrics for the same storage account to a Log Analytics workspace. In the workspace, the exported metric records show only a single total per interval, with no breakdown by ResponseType. You must make the per-dimension detail available in the workspace. What should you do?
opzione_a: Recreate the diagnostic setting and select the Transactions metric category instead of AllMetrics.
opzione_b: Extract the metric with the Azure Monitor Metrics REST API and ingest the results into the workspace by using the Logs Ingestion API.
opzione_c: Increase the retention of the workspace table so that the dimension values are preserved.
opzione_d: Install the Azure Monitor Agent on the storage account and create a data collection rule for the dimension.
spiegazione: Correct: Diagnostic settings do not currently support multidimensional metrics. Metrics with dimensions are exported as flattened, single-dimensional metrics that are aggregated across dimension values, which is exactly the behaviour observed. The documented workaround is to extract the metric manually with the Metrics REST API and import it into a Log Analytics workspace by using the Logs Ingestion API. Why the others are wrong: Metric categories other than AllMetrics aren't supported for the vast majority of Azure services; attempting to specify one returns a 'Metric category is not supported' error, and it would not restore the dimensions anyway. Retention controls how long records are kept, not whether dimension values are captured at ingestion time. The Azure Monitor Agent collects guest OS telemetry from virtual machines and cannot be installed on a platform-as-a-service storage account.
tags: azure monitor,multi-dimensional metrics,diagnostic settings,allmetrics,logs ingestion api

domanda: An engineer reports that when she sets the time picker in Azure Monitor metrics explorer to a custom 45-day range, the chart for the Percentage CPU metric of a virtual machine renders blank. The virtual machine has been running continuously for six months and the same chart displays data correctly over the last 7 days. What is the most likely cause?
opzione_a: Metrics explorer can query no more than 30 days of data on any single chart.
opzione_b: Platform metrics are retained for only 30 days, so no data exists beyond that point.
opzione_c: A diagnostic setting that sends AllMetrics to a Log Analytics workspace is required before historical metrics can be charted.
opzione_d: The time granularity is set to Automatic, which suppresses data points for ranges longer than one month.
spiegazione: Correct: Although platform metrics are stored for 93 days, metrics explorer can query a maximum of 30 days of data on any single chart. Selecting a start-to-end interval greater than 30 days produces a blank chart or a chart showing only part of the data. After selecting a 30-day interval, you can pan the chart to view the full 93-day retention window. Why the others are wrong: Platform metrics are retained for 93 days, not 30, so the data does exist. No diagnostic setting is needed to chart platform metrics in metrics explorer; platform metrics are collected automatically and a diagnostic setting is only needed to route them to other destinations. Automatic time granularity simply selects an appropriate time grain for the chosen range; it never suppresses data.

sotto_argomento: Configure log settings in Azure Monitor
domanda: You are documenting the destinations that an Azure Monitor diagnostic setting can send platform logs and platform metrics to. Which three of the following are valid diagnostic setting destinations? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
spiegazione: Correct: A diagnostic setting can send data to a Log Analytics workspace (for KQL queries, workbooks, and log alerts), an Azure Storage account (for archive, static analysis, or backup), and an Azure Event Hubs namespace (to stream data to external systems such as a third-party SIEM). Azure Monitor partner solutions are the fourth supported destination type. Why the others are wrong: An Azure Service Bus queue is not a diagnostic setting destination; Event Hubs is the streaming destination Azure Monitor supports, and the two services are commonly confused. An Azure Cosmos DB container is not a destination either; Cosmos DB is a source that can emit resource logs through its own diagnostic setting, not a target for them.

domanda: A development team plans to publish business telemetry to Azure Monitor as custom metrics so that the values can be charted in metrics explorer alongside platform metrics. Which three statements about Azure Monitor custom metrics are correct? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: A custom metric can carry a maximum of 10 dimension keys.
opzione_b: Custom metrics are retained for the same period as platform metrics.
opzione_c: A custom metric definition must be created in Azure Monitor before the first value is emitted.
opzione_d: A subscription is limited to 50,000 active time series per region.
opzione_e: Custom metrics must be enabled through a diagnostic setting before they appear in metrics explorer.
spiegazione: Correct: Azure Monitor limits custom metrics to 10 dimension keys per metric. Custom metrics are retained for the same amount of time as platform metrics, which is 93 days. The subscription quota is 50,000 total active time series per region, where an active time series is any unique combination of metric, dimension key, and dimension value published in the past 12 hours. Why the others are wrong: You do not need to predefine a custom metric; the first time you emit a custom metric, Azure Monitor automatically creates the metric definition. Diagnostic settings route platform metrics, resource logs, and the activity log to other destinations; they play no part in ingesting custom metrics, which arrive through the Application Insights SDK, the Azure Monitor Agent with a data collection rule, the Telegraf agent, or the custom metrics REST API.

sotto_argomento: Configure log settings in Azure Monitor
domanda: A security team must be able to run KQL queries against every category of resource log produced by a key vault named kv-contoso-prod, and must also be able to query the key vault's platform metrics in the same workspace. The configuration must automatically include any new log category that Microsoft adds to Key Vault in the future, and must use the fewest possible diagnostic settings. Select the appropriate option for each requirement.
opzione_a: Log category group to select: [audit | allLogs | verbose]
opzione_b: Metric category to select: [AllMetrics | ServiceApiHit | Availability]
opzione_c: Destination to select: [Azure Storage account | Log Analytics workspace | Azure Event Hubs namespace]
spiegazione: Correct: The allLogs category group collects all categories for the resource, and because Microsoft maintains the group definition, log collection is modified automatically when categories are added. AllMetrics is the metric category used to collect platform metrics through a diagnostic setting; metric categories other than AllMetrics aren't supported for the vast majority of Azure services. A Log Analytics workspace is the only destination that supports KQL log queries. A single diagnostic setting can define one destination of each type and can include both logs and metrics, so one setting is sufficient. Why the other options are wrong: The audit category group collects only the resource logs that record customer interactions with data or service settings, which is a subset of allLogs and would miss other categories. 'verbose' is not an Azure Monitor category group. ServiceApiHit and Availability are individual Key Vault metric names, not selectable diagnostic setting metric categories. An Azure Storage account destination supports archival only and an Azure Event Hubs namespace only streams data out of Azure; neither supports KQL. Two or three settings would be needed only if you were targeting multiple destinations of the same type.

domanda: You are analyzing the Percentage CPU metric for a set of virtual machines in Azure Monitor metrics explorer. You must identify the worst CPU spike within each interval and determine which individual virtual machine is responsible. Select the appropriate option for each requirement.
opzione_a: Aggregation that shows the highest value captured in each interval: [Average | Max | Count]
opzione_b: Feature that draws a separate chart line per virtual machine: [Filtering | Splitting | Y-axis lock]
opzione_c: Smallest time granularity available on the chart: [15 seconds | 1 minute | 5 minutes]
opzione_d: How the Average aggregation is produced: [Sum divided by Count | Midpoint of Min and Max | Preaggregated and stored per interval]
spiegazione: Correct: Max returns the largest value captured over the aggregation interval, which is what surfaces a spike. Splitting controls whether the chart displays separate lines for each value of a dimension, so splitting by virtual machine (or resource ID) produces one line per machine. The current minimum time granularity in metrics explorer is 1 minute, even though the underlying system may sample faster. Average is always the Sum divided by the Count; it is never stored preaggregated and is recalculated for each time granularity from the aggregated Sum and Count so that calculation errors are avoided. Why the other options are wrong: Average would smooth away the spike, and Count only reports how many measurements were captured. Filtering chooses which dimension values are included in the chart but still aggregates them into one line unless splitting is applied; Y-axis lock only changes the visible value range. 15 seconds is the interval at which the platform samples VM CPU underneath, but it is not selectable as a chart time grain; 5 minutes is a valid grain but is not the smallest. Average is not the midpoint of Min and Max, and unlike Sum, Count, Min, and Max it is not preaggregated.

sotto_argomento: Configure log settings in Azure Monitor
domanda: An auditor needs to determine which user created a specific virtual machine two years ago. Your organization has not changed any monitoring defaults on the subscription. Select the appropriate option to complete each statement about the Azure activity log.
opzione_a: Default retention of activity log events: [30 days | 90 days | 93 days]
opzione_b: Destination required to retain activity log events for two years: [Azure Monitor workspace | Log Analytics workspace | Azure Monitor metrics store]
opzione_c: Table that stores exported activity log data: [AzureActivity | AzureDiagnostics | AzureMetrics]
spiegazione: Correct: Azure retains activity log events for 90 days and then deletes them, at no charge regardless of volume. To keep them longer you create a diagnostic setting that exports the activity log to a Log Analytics workspace, where retention can be increased up to 12 years and there are no ingestion charges for activity logs. Exported activity log data lands in the AzureActivity table. Why the other options are wrong: 30 days is not an activity log retention value, and 93 days is the retention of platform and custom metrics, not of the activity log. An Azure Monitor workspace stores Prometheus metrics and is not an activity log destination; the Azure Monitor metrics store holds numeric time-series data, not log records. AzureDiagnostics is the table used by resource logs collected in Azure diagnostics collection mode, and AzureMetrics holds exported platform metrics; neither receives activity log entries.

sotto_argomento: Configure log settings in Azure Monitor
domanda: Fabrikam has an Azure Application Gateway named agw-prod deployed in the West US region in a subscription named Sub1. A central operations team owns a Log Analytics workspace named law-central in a different subscription named Sub2, in the East US region. You have appropriate Azure RBAC permissions on both subscriptions. You plan to create diagnostic settings for agw-prod. Evaluate each of the following statements and indicate whether it is true. 1. A single diagnostic setting on agw-prod can send the resource logs to two different Log Analytics workspaces. 2. law-central must be in the West US region because agw-prod is a regional resource. 3. law-central can be used as the destination even though it is in a different subscription than agw-prod.
opzione_a: A single diagnostic setting on agw-prod can send the resource logs to two different Log Analytics workspaces.
opzione_b: law-central must be in the West US region because agw-prod is a regional resource.
opzione_c: law-central can be used as the destination even though it is in a different subscription than agw-prod.
spiegazione: Statement 1 is No: a single diagnostic setting can define no more than one destination of each type. To send data to two Log Analytics workspaces you must create two separate diagnostic settings, which is permitted because each resource supports up to five settings. Statement 2 is No: the same-region requirement applies only to Azure Storage account and Azure Event Hubs destinations for regional resources. A Log Analytics workspace destination is not subject to that constraint, so law-central can remain in East US. Statement 3 is Yes: the destination does not have to be in the same subscription as the resource sending the logs, provided the user configuring the setting has appropriate Azure RBAC access to both subscriptions, which is stated in the scenario. For destinations in another Microsoft Entra tenant, Azure Lighthouse would be used.

sotto_argomento: Configure log settings in Azure Monitor
domanda: You must collect all resource log categories from a network security group named nsg-web and make them queryable with KQL. No Log Analytics workspace exists in the subscription yet. Arrange the following actions in the correct order to complete the configuration by using the Azure portal.
opzione_a: Select Save, then allow up to 90 minutes for data to begin flowing to the destination.
opzione_b: Create the Log Analytics workspace that will receive the data.
opzione_c: Select Add diagnostic setting and provide a descriptive name for the setting.
opzione_d: On the nsg-web menu, select Diagnostic settings in the Monitoring section.
opzione_e: Select the allLogs category group, select Send to Log Analytics workspace, and choose the workspace.
spiegazione: Correct order: (1) Create the Log Analytics workspace, because the destination resource must already exist before you create the diagnostic setting. (2) Open Diagnostic settings from the Monitoring section of the nsg-web resource menu, which is the documented entry point for creating a resource-scoped setting. (3) Select Add diagnostic setting and give it a descriptive name. (4) Choose the allLogs category group so that every resource log category is collected, then select Send to Log Analytics workspace and pick the workspace. (5) Save the setting; after creation, data should start flowing to the selected destination within 90 minutes, and the destination table is created automatically when the first records arrive. Common ordering errors: attempting to select the workspace before it exists causes it to be unavailable in the destination picker, and naming the setting is only possible after selecting Add diagnostic setting.
tags: azure monitor,diagnostic settings,network security group,alllogs,log analytics workspace,portal
